title: NTFS Structural Corruption and Offline Repair Requests
exclusions: Reports unique Microsoft-Windows-Ntfs System events 55 and 98. Microsoft documents 55 as detected file-system structure that is corrupt and unusable and 98 as a volume requiring offline Full Chkdsk. A row does not prove physical disk failure, data loss, successful/failed self-healing, completed repair, root cause, or current unavailability; storage, driver, filter, SAN and interrupted-I/O conditions require investigation. It excludes other NTFS IDs, ReFS/FAT, generic disk/StorPort events, SMART telemetry, corruption visible only to an application, and events missing host/record identity. Event payload fields vary by OS/message version, so the analytic does not depend on an assumed `DriveName` or `CorruptionType`. The closed 15-minute interval, five-minute delay and severity routing are local choices. Missing System feeds, duplicates, late events and lost original Computer are source-health conditions. This UC does not run chkdsk/Repair-Volume, dismount a volume, fail over storage, replace a disk, restore data, or attest backup integrity.
evidence: Retain the version-controlled `windows_ntfs_corruption_repair_required` search, schedule, ACL and results; each result with host/EventRecordID, event ID/classification, provider, available volume/device/corruption fields, rendered message, source metadata and index time; raw System XML; expected-host and duplicate-route health; OS/storage/volume inventory; adjacent Ntfs, Disk, StorPort, stornvme, volmgr and WHEA records; `fsutil repair`/`Repair-Volume`/chkdsk output only when change-approved; backup/restore status; incident/change records, alert delivery, disposition and dated positive, negative, duplicate, delay, field-version and upgrade tests. This documentation review generated no corruption, repair, search, alert or runtime evidence.

controlTest.positiveScenario: In an isolated index under fixed bounds, ingest one XML System event from provider `Microsoft-Windows-Ntfs`, EventCode 55, Computer `fs-lab-01`, EventRecordID `68001`, VolumeName `D:`, and a rendered message containing the documented corrupt/unusable text. Expect exactly one row with `issue_class=structural_corruption_detected`, severity `critical`, host/record identity, volume and message. Independently replay EventCode 98 with record `68002`; expect `issue_class=offline_full_chkdsk_requested`.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Expect zero rows for EventCode 140, Disk 153, ReFS corruption, provider mismatch, missing host or EventRecordID, wrong source/source type, newest excluded five minutes, and duplicate copies of the same host/EventRecordID. Verify numeric/string ID normalization and that a missing VolumeName still returns a valid row with `volume=unknown`. Source health must separately report missing hosts, duplicates, delay and extraction drift.

dataSources: Native Windows **System** channel events from provider `Microsoft-Windows-Ntfs`: Event ID 55 and 98. Collect XML with Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (Splunkbase 742) to deployment-choice `index=wineventlog`, exact `sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog`, `source=XmlWinEventLog:System`. Required: `_time, _indextime, Computer|dest|host, EventCode|EventID, Provider_Name|ProviderName|SourceName, EventRecordID|RecordNumber`; preserve Message/RenderedDescription and any VolumeName, DriveName, DeviceName, CorruptionState, RepairDetail fields present in raw XML. Microsoft event text and local XML are authoritative; adjacent storage events are corroboration.
app: Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (`Splunk_TA_windows`, Splunkbase 742) for System XML collection and field knowledge; a local operations content app owns the analytic, source health, fixtures, dashboard and `windows_ntfs_event_exceptions.csv`.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog" source="XmlWinEventLog:System" EventCode IN (55,98) earliest=-20m@m latest=-5m@m
| eval event_id=tonumber(coalesce(EventCode,EventID)), provider=lower(trim(coalesce(Provider_Name,ProviderName,SourceName))), destination=lower(trim(coalesce(Computer,dest,host))), event_record_id=trim(tostring(coalesce(EventRecordID,RecordNumber))), volume=trim(coalesce(VolumeName,DriveName,DeviceName,"unknown")), rendered_message=coalesce(Message,RenderedDescription,"")
| where in(event_id,55,98) AND in(provider,"microsoft-windows-ntfs","ntfs") AND len(destination)>0 AND len(event_record_id)>0
| eval issue_class=case(event_id=55,"structural_corruption_detected",event_id=98,"offline_full_chkdsk_requested"), severity=case(event_id=55,"critical",event_id=98,"high")
| stats count AS duplicate_count min(_time) AS event_time max(_indextime) AS last_indextime values(volume) AS volumes values(CorruptionState) AS corruption_states values(RepairDetail) AS repair_details values(rendered_message) AS rendered_messages values(source) AS observed_sources values(sourcetype) AS observed_sourcetypes by destination event_record_id event_id provider issue_class severity
| where duplicate_count=1
| eval aggregation_window_minutes=15, close_delay_minutes=5, analytic_interpretation="native NTFS corruption/repair-required event; investigate volume and storage path; event alone does not prove hardware failure or repair outcome", use_case="UC-1.2.68"
| table event_time destination event_record_id event_id provider issue_class severity volumes corruption_states repair_details rendered_messages observed_sources observed_sourcetypes last_indextime aggregation_window_minutes close_delay_minutes analytic_interpretation use_case
| sort 0 -severity -event_time destination
description: Reports one unique host/EventRecordID row for each NTFS Event 55 or 98 in a closed 15-minute interval, classifying structural corruption detection versus an offline Full Chkdsk request. The row preserves available volume/message context but does not infer repair completion or hardware cause.
value: Rapid, exact routing of NTFS corruption and offline-repair requests helps owners protect service availability, preserve evidence, validate backups and coordinate storage/volume repair before additional writes or an unplanned restart complicate recovery. Separating native event meaning from root-cause inference prevents premature disk replacement or unsafe automated repair.
implementation: Collect the System channel as XML from every in-scope Windows host and validate native provider, IDs, original Computer and EventRecordID. Save `windows_ntfs_corruption_repair_required`, run every 15 minutes over the closed slice, and notify on any result. Before repair, verify raw event/message, volume identity, service/cluster role, storage path, backup status and adjacent I/O telemetry; execute Microsoft-supported diagnostics only through an approved outage and recovery plan.
visualization: Operations dashboard `Windows — NTFS Corruption and Repair Requests`: expected-host, delay and duplicate health first; active results by issue class, host and volume; timeline; affected asset/service/cluster table; and full SPL result fields. Drill down to raw System XML, adjacent Ntfs/Disk/StorPort/stornvme/volmgr/WHEA events, storage/SAN alerts, volume inventory, backup/restore verification and approved repair/change records. Never label Event 98 as completed self-healing.
schema: Microsoft-Windows-Ntfs System Event IDs 55 and 98 native XML
dataModelAcceleration: No standard CIM dataset preserves the specific Ntfs provider, native 55/98 meanings, host/EventRecordID identity and payload/message fields needed here. The Change data model is not semantically equivalent. No `cimSpl` is claimed; any summary must retain exact native gates and pass raw-result parity.

knownFalsePositives:
These events are operationally real; a “false positive” is duplicate telemetry, an already-owned condition, or a trigger whose root cause is not physical disk failure.

1. **Known volume repair incident** — repeated 55/98 can occur while a ticketed outage/repair is pending. Match exact host, volume/device, incident, owner, UTC window and latest raw event; keep escalation for new IDs/volumes or post-repair recurrence.
2. **SAN/path/controller interruption** — transient I/O completion failures can lead to NTFS symptoms without a failed local disk. Correlate StorPort/Disk events, MPIO/path state, array alerts, LUN mapping, firmware/driver and storage-team evidence.
3. **Snapshot, backup, filter or security driver interaction** — VSS/backup/antivirus/filter drivers can affect volume I/O. Validate product job/session, filter stack, vendor case, exact volume/time and successful recovery; never assume causality from timing alone.
4. **Planned crash, failover, snapshot rollback or unsafe shutdown test** — an approved resilience exercise can expose a pre-existing dirty/corrupt state. Match change/test ID, host/volume, operator, expected events and recovery verification.
5. **Cloned or restored test image with historical System events** — backfill can deliver old records. Compare event time, `_indextime`, EventRecordID, image provenance and current volume state; fix backfill routing rather than suppress current corruption.
6. **Direct plus WEF duplication** — identical host/EventRecordID copies are collection defects. Repair source authority; the base rule excludes duplicates while health preserves them.

**Safe suppression:** apply lookup windows_ntfs_event_exceptions.csv after base detection. Require exact `destination,volume,event_id`, incident/change ID, numeric inclusive `valid_from_epoch`, exclusive `valid_until_epoch`, owner, approver, purpose and escalation rule for recurrence. Reject wildcard hosts/volumes and open-ended dates. Suppress duplicate notification only; retain raw findings and never suppress source health or a new EventRecordID after declared repair.
reviewer: documentation-only editorial review against primary Microsoft NTFS corruption/repair guidance and primary Splunk Windows XML documentation; event semantics, collection, SPL, fixtures, source health, dashboards, exceptions, diagnostics and recovery were specified but not executed or Microsoft/storage/Windows/Splunk-SME signed

cost.search_load_notes: Events 55/98 should be rare. The query uses index/source/Event ID predicates over one closed 15-minute slice and aggregates by native identity. Storage cost is dominated by the broader System feed.

detailedImplementation:
## Define ownership and safety

Assign Windows platform, storage/SAN, application/service, backup/recovery, Splunk collection/content and incident owners. Inventory every in-scope host with canonical Computer, OS build, physical/virtual/cloud placement, volume-to-service and volume-to-disk/LUN mapping, cluster/failover role, storage owner, backup policy, maintenance window and forwarding path. Restrict the operations dashboard with a Splunk role because paths and infrastructure details are sensitive.

Microsoft documents Event 55 as file-system structure detected corrupt and unusable and Event 98 as a volume that needs to be taken offline for Full Chkdsk. Neither proves a physical disk failed. Event 98 is not “self-healing completed.” Hardware, incomplete I/O, drivers, filters, SAN paths and other conditions must be evaluated. Never schedule an automatic dismount, repair or restart from an event alone.

## Collect the native System event

Deploy Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows from Splunkbase 742. In a managed `inputs.conf`, enable `[WinEventLog://System]`, `renderXml=true`, and local `index=wineventlog`. Verify `sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog` and `source=XmlWinEventLog:System`; these exact contracts must be tested after add-on upgrades. Preserve original Computer and EventRecordID through WEF.

Inspect **Event Viewer > Windows Logs > System** and Splunk together:

```spl
index=wineventlog sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog" source="XmlWinEventLog:System" (EventCode=55 OR EventCode=98) earliest=-7d
| table _time _indextime Computer EventRecordID Provider_Name EventCode VolumeName DriveName DeviceName CorruptionState RepairDetail Message RenderedDescription
```

Compare raw XML and rendered text on each supported OS. Provider should be Microsoft-Windows-Ntfs (legacy extraction can expose Ntfs). Payload fields vary, so host/record/provider/ID are mandatory and volume/message fields are retained opportunistically. Do not regex localized rendered text as the primary identifier.

## Maintain source and identity health

Create an expected-host monitor for absent/stale System data, abnormal event-time delay, channel clear/full, forwarder/WEF backlog, unknown host, missing provider/Computer/EventRecordID, future timestamps, extraction drift and duplicate Computer/EventRecordID across direct/WEF routes. A host without recent 55/98 is healthy only if its general System feed is current.

EventRecordID is channel-local and may reset after a log clear. Use Computer, record ID, bounded event time and raw hash during incident correlation. The base rule requires a single observed identity; duplicated records are excluded from notifications but must remain visible in source health.

## Configure and understand the saved search

Save the SPL as `windows_ntfs_corruption_repair_required`, schedule every 15 minutes, and trigger when result count is greater than zero. `earliest=-20m@m latest=-5m@m` scans a closed 15-minute event-time interval after five minutes for arrival. Measure p99 forwarding delay and increase close delay without overlapping slices.

The query applies index/source/Event ID predicates, normalizes provider/host/record identity, and coalesces optional volume/message fields without making them required. Event 55 receives `structural_corruption_detected`; Event 98 receives `offline_full_chkdsk_requested`. The stats stage verifies uniqueness and retains source fields. One row is one native event, not one disk and not proof of unresolved current corruption.

No Change/Performance CIM acceleration is equivalent. A local summary can optimize only if it preserves provider, native ID, Computer/EventRecordID, payload/message, closed interval and raw parity.

## Validate without damaging data

Replay the two documented synthetic XML fixtures under absolute time bounds and assert all fields. Run each negative independently: other NTFS/storage IDs, provider mismatch, missing identity, wrong source, newest-delay and duplicates. Test absent volume, localized message, uppercase provider, WEF destination preservation, EventRecordID reuse after clear and earliest/latest boundaries. Confirm source-health findings separately.

Do not deliberately corrupt a production volume. In an isolated disposable lab, use prebuilt synthetic events for routine tests. If storage engineers approve a realistic corruption/repair exercise, snapshot disposable media, document expected data loss, capture raw events and commands, and destroy/reset the lab afterward. Documentation review does not count as execution.

Measure System ingest, search runtime, alert delivery, dashboard ACL/drilldown, ticket routing and exception expiry. Keep status draft until platform, storage, backup and Splunk owners sign source coverage and recovery runbooks.

## Triage and recover

Alert title: `NTFS <issue_class> on <destination> (<volumes>)`. Analysts first verify raw provider/ID/record, event age, original host and source health. Resolve volume to service, cluster and physical disk/LUN; inspect adjacent Ntfs 50/140, Disk 7/51/129/153/157 as applicable, StorPort/stornvme/volmgr/WHEA, array/path/controller alerts and filter-driver changes. Confirm current mount/read/write state and recent restart/failover.

Validate backups and an actual restore path before invasive repair. Coordinate application quiescence, cluster ownership, snapshots, free space, outage and rollback. Use `chkdsk`, `Repair-Volume` or `fsutil repair` only under Microsoft/vendor guidance and an approved change; command choice depends on state and can require offline access/restart. Preserve output and post-repair Event Logs. Repeated events after repair require renewed escalation.

Apply lookup windows_ntfs_event_exceptions.csv only after base results. Preserve every raw event and health defect. Review incidents daily and remove exceptions immediately after repair validation.

## Troubleshoot

- No results: verify System input, XML rendering, provider spelling, event IDs, index permissions, forwarder/WEF queues and native channel retention.
- Volume unknown: inspect raw XML and localized message; use host volume inventory rather than inventing a field extraction.
- Duplicate count: identify direct plus WEF routes or replay and restore one authority.
- Event 55 but healthy disk: investigate filesystem, I/O path, drivers, filters and SAN; the event never asserted physical failure.
- Event 98 after repair: verify which volume was repaired, command exit/output, restart/offline requirement and new EventRecordID.
- CIM returns nothing: expected; this native fault has no claimed equivalent.
grandmaExplanation: We watch for Windows saying an NTFS volume is structurally damaged or must be taken offline for a full check. The alert helps specialists protect data and plan repair, but it does not automatically blame the physical disk.
hardware: Windows systems using NTFS volumes and generating provider Microsoft-Windows-Ntfs events in the System channel. ReFS/FAT, non-Windows filesystems, storage arrays, hypervisor-only telemetry and hosts without complete System collection require separate monitoring.
